chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who had an Umm al-Walad (concubine who bore him a child), and he married her to a man, and she bore him a boy. Then the man died, and she returned to her master. Is it permissible for him to have sexual relations with her? He said: She observes the waiting period (Iddah) from the deceased husband for four months and ten days. Then he can have relations with her by virtue of ownership (Milk), without a new marriage contract.

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine who bore her master a child
key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: Waiting period after death or divorce

ai.seo_question: What is the Iddah and marital status of a concubine who was married off by her master after her husband dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the specific legal status of an Umm al-Walad married by her master, distinguishing her Iddah period from that of a free woman. It establishes that upon completion of the waiting period, the master resumes sexual rights through ownership (Milk al-Yamin) without requiring a new marriage contract, a ruling derived from the principle that her marriage was an extension of her master's authority. This highlights the flexibility of marital structures in early Shia jurisprudence regarding concubinage and slave ownership.
